## Active

### D-004 — Profile fields reuse party.person, core.property and access_user

> _2026-08-21 · realm/blong-access · active_

The profile feature needed somewhere to keep a display name, a preferred language and an email
address, and new columns were rejected in favour of tables that already exist. The display name
reuses `party.person` when the user has one and falls back to a no-personal-data path when they do
not; `preferredLanguage` is a `core.property` row keyed `(resourceId='preferredLanguage')`;
`emailAddress` stays on `access_user` because that is where login already reads it. No schema
migration was needed, so the feature could be deployed against the existing databases instead of
rebuilding them.

### D-005 — Self-service profile actions skip the RBAC action-list check

> _2026-08-21 · realm/blong-access · active_

`access.profile.get/edit/password.change` must work for any logged-in user, but `access.*` handlers
normally require the caller to hold the matching action. Instead of seeding a role grant for every
user, the three handlers follow the `login.token.revoke` pattern: bearer authentication plus
`skipAuthorize`, so the RBAC action-list check is skipped. That keeps the self-service surface
independent of the role model — a user is not locked out of their own profile until an administrator
grants something — and it avoids role-grant seed changes.

### D-006 — Password change keeps the current session instead of revoking it

> _2026-08-21 · realm/blong-access · active_

Changing your own password does not revoke the current session: the decision was to keep the user
logged in, and the only constraint attached is the active `access_policy` minimum length, which the
handler relies on rather than re-implementing. Revoking would have meant a re-login after every
password change and would have made the profile page's own submit flow fail against the session it
was using.

### D-007 — The Bulgarian language test lives only in blong-access

> _2026-08-21 · realm/blong-access · active_

Rather than adding a translated Playwright test to every suite, the test lives in blong-access: it
sets `preferredLanguage='bg'` through the test hook, calls `page.reload()` to re-trigger the boot
restore (which returns the language), asserts that the menu and profile render in Bulgarian,
screenshots `profile-bg.png`, and restores `'en'` so the shared dev database and the other
screenshots stay stable.

### D-008 — Realm RBAC merges are additive, so their order does not matter

> _2026-08-23 · realm/blong-access · active_

The merge handler is insert-only on conflict (`coreResourceEnsure`) and uses `core.triple.merge` for
edges, so the access file and a realm's own file can be applied in ANY order and repeatedly without
creating duplicates. Verified end to end by deleting commanderAdmin's 22 `hasAction` edges in the
dev database and restarting the backend: the commander merge file re-seeded all 22 plus the
`Admin → commanderAdmin` `hasCapability` grant, and testAdmin's `commander.source.list` still
returned all 8 sources with RBAC pruning intact, while the access `accessModelAdmin` (24 actions)
was untouched.

### D-041 — blong-access wires the switcher, blong-party stays unaffected

> _2026-08-21 · realm/blong-access · active_

blong-access configures `languages: [{value:'en',label:'English'},{value:'bg',label:'Български'}]`
next to its existing `translations`. blong-party is intentionally left alone: with no `languages`
and no `translations` the switcher renders nothing, so the party menubar baselines are unchanged.

### D-042 — CRUD actions collapse to one entity row in the capability pivot

> _2026-08-19 · realm/blong-access · active_

The capability editor's action tab should not list `accessCapabilityRemove` and its siblings as
separate rows, and the user confirmed the rule applies to ALL entities: any action whose name ends
in a standard CRUD suffix collapses to one entity row. It is implemented with a custom
`access.crudEntity` dropdown served by a new realm handler `adapter/db/accessDropdownList.ts` that
calls `super.exec` for the auto per-table dropdowns and adds the entity list derived from
`access_action` plus `core_resource` (the distinct `access<Entity>` prefixes of standard-CRUD
actions); the model pivot uses
`{dropdown:'access.crudEntity', join:{value:'entityName', label:'entityName'}}`, and
`crudActionParts`/`crudPivotActionIds` map ticked cells to ensure plus sync `access<Entity><Pred>`
action edges. Non-CRUD actions live in an `otherAction` card inside the Action tab. Trade-off
accepted: overriding `access.dropdown.list` means every access dropdown call pays the extra
`access_action` query, guarded by returning the base on a missing `qb`; the list reflects only
entities that have at least one registered CRUD action, which is correct because you can only grant
what exists. Verified live (entity rows with full CRUD for accessUser/accessRole/accessCapability,
Find for the others, plus the Other Actions card) and by Playwright 19/19, the tap flow and both
packages' lint.

### D-063 — Closing your own session needs no permission, another's does

> _2026-08-20 · realm/blong-access · active_

`access.session.close` closes your OWN session (`params.sessionId === $meta.auth.sessionId`, the JWT
`ses` claim) with no permission at all — a valid token suffices — so logout, revoke and
refresh-reuse detection keep working for every user. Closing ANY OTHER session requires the
`access.session.close` action in `$meta.auth.actions`, and a violation throws the new
`access.session.closeForbidden` (403) error. Callers that close another session (test seeds, token
exchange reuse) pass `{...$meta, auth: {...}}` to satisfy it, and refresh marks the session it
closes as its own through `auth.sessionId`. "Require the action always" was rejected because
self-close is a core logout primitive every logged-in user must have.

### D-064 — A role that collided on roleBit silently overwrote Admin

> _2026-08-21 · realm/blong-access · active_

On a fresh database blong-access, gateway and kopi failed their tests while a second run succeeded.
The blong-access test seed creates the test-only `NoLogin` role through `accessAuthorizationMerge`,
which hardcodes `extraColumns: {roleBit: 0}`; `access_role.roleBit` is a UNIQUE key and
`coreResourceEnsure` inserted with `.onConflict(key).merge()` (MySQL `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`),
which fires on ANY unique-key conflict — so the `NoLogin` insert overwrote the `Admin` row and
deleted Admin from `access_role`, breaking every downstream join until the next run's prod seed
re-inserted it. Two changes: `NoLogin` is pre-seeded with the free `roleBit: 5` in
`core/blong-access/meta/db/1-accessRoleMerge.yaml` (following the documented rule that a new role
must be pre-seeded there because the merge handler hardcodes bit 0), and `coreResourceEnsure` was
hardened to `.onConflict(key).ignore()` (`INSERT IGNORE`) so a secondary unique-key conflict can
never silently overwrite an existing row. Pre-seeding was chosen over making
`accessAuthorizationMerge` auto-assign roleBits (a bigger contract change) and over `.ignore()`
alone (which would have silently orphaned the entity row). Verified by dropping the database: the
first run passes for all four packages and the database shows Admin(0) through Guest(4), then
NoLogin(5); the second run is idempotent.
